newsitem.title: POLAND: OSCE monitors concerned on Armenian poll integrity.
newsitem.headline: OSCE monitors concerned on Armenian poll integrity.

text.p: OSCE observers have reported "very serious breaches" of Armenia's election law which they say could call into question last week's re-election of President Levon Ter-Petrosyan.

"The OSCE/ODIHR International Observer Mission has concluded that very serious breaches in the election law took place during the vote tabulation process, the verification process and the aggregation of results, causing concern for the overall integrity of the election process," the organisation said in a statement issued to Reuters on Thursday.

The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) monitored the September 22 poll and initially reported that breaches in the law during the poll did not seem to provide cause for materially affecting the election outcome.

But its Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights (ODIHR) in Warsaw, after further study, said particular concern was raised by a disparity of 22,013 between the number of people who voted and the number of voter coupons registered in the official results.

"Particularly given the fact...Ter-Petrosyan only passed the 50 percent threshold by 21,941 votes, the inaccuracies in the verification process can only contribute to a lack of confidence in the overall electoral process and could even question the results of the first round of balloting," it said.
The discrepancy was most marked in the capital Yerevan.
On Sunday Ter-Petrosyan, 51, was declared winner of the election with 51.8 percent of the vote, just above the level needed to avoid a runoff with challenger Vazgen Manukyan who took 41.3 percent.

Manukyan has gone into hiding and his supporters have staged protests alleging vote-rigging, while diplomats and opposition politicians in the former Soviet republic have accused Ter-Petrosyan of using the protests to jail opponents and stifle dissent.
The OSCE said it would submit a final report shortly but urged a review of Armenia's election law to prevent future irregularities.
"Clearly those who do not administer the law correctly should be sanctioned," it said.
The statement said irregularities included inconsistent criteria for invalidating ballots in three precincts, a process which had favoured Ter-Petrosyan.
In some places unauthorised people, notably Interior Ministry personnel, were present in polling stations in a clear breach of the law.

The OSCE report cited consultations between officials, Ter-Petrosyan supporters and precinct electoral commission chairmen, including a case of tampering with a voter coupon box which was later found to contain 200 unsigned and unnumbered coupons.

Ballot boxes were left unguarded, regional election commissions made negligible attempts to verify precinct results, and observers were made unwelcome, it said, but added: "These instances were not repeated throughout the country."
The statement criticised the Central Electoral Commission for a delay in issuing regulations on verification of results, leaving lower bodies unclear how to proceed.

It said that, after clashes on September 25 between Manukyan supporters and riot police, "most regional election commissions became highly partisan which clearly affected any attempt to conduct the verification process."
